A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COSMOS research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, added, and removed material.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, robustness, ablation, generation-quality, and inference-time experiments, including additional Wikipedia experiments in Appendix C.2.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and additionally reports OpenWebText model-scaling and generation comparisons, plus memorization scores.

M1.justification: The frozen BERT encoder, compressor/decompressor, reconstruction and MSE objectives, augmentations, self-conditioning, and diffusion procedure are unchanged. The additional depths and latent lengths are experimental configurations of the retained method.

E1.justification: Section 8 adds OpenWebText training and evaluation for 128-token and 512-token generation, substantially extending empirical coverage to web text. The original four generative tasks and Wikipedia autoencoder training remain; removal of the Wikipedia result tables does not establish that Wikipedia is no longer used.

E2.justification: v2 adds GIDD as an evaluated comparator alongside TEncDM in the OpenWebText comparison, Table 6. The comparator sets in the retained four-task comparisons are unchanged; other newly cited methods are discussed without reported evaluations.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a controlled 12/24/48-layer depth study, approximately 0.12/0.25/0.5B parameters, with a fixed autoencoder and 128 latents. It also tests 256 versus 512 latents for 512-token OpenWebText generation and adds MEM as an evaluation metric. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds model-depth sensitivity, long-sequence compression comparisons, and memorization diagnostics. It removes v1 Appendix C.2's Wikipedia component ablation and latent-length sweep, Tables 7–8. The ROCStories ablations, perturbation analyses, and variational-prior study remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten evaluation repetitions with different seeds and mean/standard-deviation reporting, plus five independent timing runs. Existing uncertainty entries are retained. The new OpenWebText tables provide point estimates without introducing a revised statistical procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds MEM entries and OpenWebText results: depth-sweep MAUVE rises from 0.849 to 0.923, and Table 6 reports 0.702 for COSMOS N=512 versus 0.286 for GIDD. The accompanying prose instead says 0.792. v1's Wikipedia Tables 7–8 disappear, while retained benchmark scores remain unchanged. These additions are not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The diffusion equations, latent-space formulations, robustness measurements, and appendix variational/KL mathematics are retained. No new theorem, proof, or formal definition is introduced; MEM is named without a mathematical definition.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the claims about compressed smooth latents, competitive generation, and faster inference. Changing the abstract's compression wording from 'by 8×' to 'up to 8×' aligns it with the scope already stated elsewhere in v1.

C2.justification: Section 8 adds interpretations that greater denoiser capacity improves generation with a fixed autoencoder and that compression trades fidelity for compactness on OpenWebText. The Wikipedia-specific interpretations disappear with Appendix C.2. Existing mechanism explanations and limitations remain, including the now-outdated description of roughly 130M-parameter backbones.

D1.justification: v2 newly supplies a code-release statement and GitHub link. Existing implementation details, hardware, hyperparameters, training durations, and timing instructions are retained. The additions do not provide an operational definition of MEM or OpenWebText-specific training-budget and split details.

R1.justification: New Appendix B substantially expands related work across Gaussian embedding, simplex, masked, and latent diffusion. It adds discussion and citations covering masked diffusion training, discrete guidance, remasking, and GIDD, plus the OpenWebText reference. The original positioning relative to LD4LG, PLANNER, and TEncDM remains.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section organization are retained. v2 adds Section 8, a related-work appendix, acknowledgements, and conference/corresponding-author text, with associated renumbering. It corrects Section 6.2's table reference but leaves a broken '??' reference to the removed Wikipedia analysis.

P2.justification: Table 4 gains a MEM column, two OpenWebText tables are added, and two Wikipedia tables are removed. Figures 1–6 retain their content and designs. Other displays undergo limited resizing, reflow, and relocation, including separating the unconditional sample tables across pages.

improvement.justification: The OpenWebText experiments broaden empirical support, while expanded related work and the code link improve context and access. However, v2 removes useful Wikipedia ablation evidence, retains a broken reference to it, and leaves MEM and OpenWebText protocols insufficiently specified. The 0.702 versus 0.792 MAUVE contradiction further weakens reporting. These limitations constrain the evidential value of the additions, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
